- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly, especially if price is trending upward.
- Model often overshoots after a recent spike in price — cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.3–0.6), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — adjust forecast toward recent 5–7 day average if price is drifting.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment changes direction within 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may overfit to recent highs — apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid “overbought” bias.
- If sentiment is negative and price is rising, model may misread momentum — increase forecast slightly to reflect sentiment reversal potential.
